body.en:
Question B-006-004-006.

Why the correct answer is right: RG-58 is smaller and usually lossier than RG-213 for the same frequency and length. With the same transmitter power, more power is lost in the RG-58 feedline, so less RF power reaches the antenna to be radiated.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "More RF power is radiated from the antenna": Switching to the lossier cable cannot increase radiated power when transmitter output and antenna are unchanged.
- sourceIndex 2: "SWR at the antenna increases": The antenna feed-point SWR is set by the antenna impedance compared with the line impedance, not by the cable being RG-213 or RG-58 if both are nominal 50-ohm coax.
- sourceIndex 3: "SWR at the antenna decreases": A lossier line can make a station-end SWR meter look different, but it does not improve the actual mismatch at the antenna feed point.
